Unit titling gives each dwelling on a dual occupancy its own separate title - the step that turns a construction project into two assets you can sell independently.

Your block qualifies.

Both dwellings must be built and have a Certificate for Occupancy and Use before the unit title can be registered. You cannot sell bare land - construction comes first. The previous 120m² size limit on one dwelling has been removed from 1 July 2026.

Card title: Sell off part of your land (Block subdivision)
Possible copy:
Block subdivision splits your block into two separate Crown leases under the Planning Act 2023 - your home stays on one, the new block becomes independently sellable as bare land.

From 1 July 2026, block subdivision is now permitted in RZ1 for the first time.

A DA is required. The new block must demonstrate it can accommodate a compliant dwelling. Access, frontage and site dimensions all affect whether a layout is achievable - a registered town planner can confirm what your block can support.

Note: this is different from unit titling under the Unit Titles Act 2001, which is covered in the card above. Block subdivision creates separate Crown leases; unit titling creates separate titles over constructed dwellings. Different processes, different outcomes.

What limits you is design, not a number. All buildings combined cannot exceed 45% site coverage. Maximum building height is 2 storeys. The number of dwellings that can fit on your block depends on those constraints, your block's shape, setbacks, trees, and the Missing Middle Housing Design Guide.
